title: Go: Race Detection
description: Use Go's built-in race detector to find and fix data races in concurrent programs.

steps.title: Introduce a data race
steps.description: Write a program where two goroutines write to the same map without synchronization. Use `go func() { m[key] = val }()` patterns. Print the map length after both goroutines finish using `fmt.Printf("Map length: %d\n", len(m))`.
hints: Concurrent writes to a map are a data race
Even concurrent read+write to map is a race

verification.failureMessage: Print the map length after concurrent writes.

steps.title: Fix with mutex
steps.description: Add a `sync.Mutex` to protect the map. Wrap all writes in `mu.Lock()` / `mu.Unlock()`. Use `defer mu.Unlock()` for safety. Print the map size after concurrent access using `fmt.Printf("Mutex map size: %d\n", len(m))`.
hints: defer unlock ensures release even on panic

steps.title: Race on shared counter
steps.description: Create 10 goroutines that each increment a shared counter 1000 times without synchronization. After all complete (using time.Sleep), print the final count. Show the race with `fmt.Printf("Expected: %d, Got: %d\n", expected, counter)`.
hints: Counter++ is not atomic: it's read-modify-write
The -race flag makes binaries 5-10x slower but catches races

verification.failureMessage: Print expected vs actual counter value.

steps.title: Fix with atomic operations
steps.description: Replace the counter with `sync/atomic.Int64`. Use `atomic.AddInt64(&counter, 1)`. Wait for all goroutines with `sync.WaitGroup`. Print the final count using `fmt.Printf("Atomic counter: %d\n", counter.Load())`.
hints: atomic.Int64 has Add, Load, Store methods

verification.failureMessage: Print the atomic counter's final value.
